raw:
Seraphel has not returned from the chapel. You take a leather chair near the fire and open the primer across your knee.

At the low table, Dena plays one-handed with practiced irritation, her splinted wrist supported on a cushion. Rashid has been dealt into the game at last; he studies his cards while Thessaly watches Mara’s turn with grave concentration.

“You can’t change the value of a card halfway through,” Dena says.

“I haven’t,” Thessaly replies. “I have clarified its potential.”

“That is changing it.”

Rashid’s mouth twitches. “I’m beginning to understand why no one invites fae to tax negotiations.”

The fire settles with a soft collapse of coals. You read while the game continues around you, occasionally punctuated by Dena’s dry complaints and the shuffle of cards.
